item.title: China's cotton know-how takes root in Central Asia
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
URUMQI, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Several hundred kilometers from Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan, cotton plants in a 1,000-mu (about 66.67 hectares) demonstration field are approaching one meter in height, each bearing 8 to 10 bolls. For Song Meizhen, chief scientist of a high-quality cotton research team at the Institute of Western Agriculture under the Chinese Academy of Agricultural Sciences, the crop is developing as expected. "Given the current growth and field management, the field is well on track to exceed the target of 550 kilograms of seed cotton per mu this year," Song said. This high-standard cotton seed breeding demonstration field is jointly operated by Xinjiang Huaxing Investment Group and the institute. From surveying the land and selecting varieties before spring planting to designing cultivation methods and setting technical standards for sowing and field management, Chinese researchers have been involved throughout the process. They have also provided regular video guidance and remote technical support. The project combines high-quality cotton varieties with a range of techniques already widely used in northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, including drip irrigation under plastic film, denser planting designed to improve light use, and mechanized harvesting. Song said the cooperation endeavor is aimed at introducing a package of Chinese cotton-growing technologies and management practices to Uzbekistan. Xinjiang is China's largest cotton-producing region. In 2025, it produced 6.17 million tonnes of cotton, accounting for 92.8 percent of the national total. The region's cotton sector is already among the world's most mechanized, with an overall mechanization rate for cultivation and harvesting surpassing 97 percent. At a smart cotton field jointly developed by the Xinjiang Changji National Agricultural High-tech Industry Demonstration Zone and the institute, weather stations and soil-moisture sensors collect field data around the clock, helping growers manage irrigation, fertilizer and other field operations more precisely. According to the institute, the system can save more than 10 percent of water and nearly 20 percent of fertilizer per mu while increasing yields by over 10 percent. Similarities in climate, water and soil conditions between Xinjiang and Central Asian countries have laid the groundwork for cross-border adoption of improved cotton varieties, cultivation techniques and agricultural machinery. Shadman Namazov, an academician of the Uzbek Academy of Sciences who has visited the Changji demonstration zone several times, said Chinese cotton-growing techniques have brought improvements in planting density, water use, yields and quality compared with traditional local practices. He cited precision irrigation and fertilizer use, mechanized operations and modern field management, saying these technologies were scientifically grounded and could be replicated on a wider scale. Namazov added that the use of Chinese techniques in Uzbekistan has helped raise cotton yields while reducing production costs, contributing to higher incomes for local growers. These cooperation efforts are also translating into stronger demand for Chinese cotton seeds and agricultural machinery in Central Asia. Hilltide, a Xinjiang-based seed industry company, sells cotton seeds and provides related technical services in Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan and Kyrgyzstan. Company executive Lu Yang said its cotton seed exports to Central Asia rose from 800 tonnes during the sales season from late 2024 to early 2025 to 1,500 tonnes during the season from late 2025 to early 2026. Lu revealed that the company's cotton seeds have maintained a market share of more than 70 percent in its Central Asian markets, attributing the growth to high-yield, stress-resistant varieties and technical services provided in addition to the seeds. Chinese cotton pickers are gaining ground in Central Asia as well. The Xinjiang branch of China Railway Construction Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. dispatched a batch of new four-row box-type cotton pickers to Central Asia in early July. The company said its cotton pickers have been developed to suit planting patterns and harvesting conditions in Central Asia, and orders from the region account for more than 70 percent of its production capacity this year. At Xinjiang Boshiran Intelligent Agricultural Machinery Co., Ltd., Vice President Feng Guang said Chinese high-end cotton pickers can match leading international products in harvesting efficiency while costing about half as much as comparable European and U.S. machines. Feng said a high level of domestically produced components, shorter delivery times and more timely after-sales service have also helped Chinese machines meet demand in Central Asian markets. The company has seen a sharp increase in overseas orders since last year, he added. Alongside business exchanges, research cooperation has also deepened. Since 2023, Chinese institutions have worked with agricultural research institutes across all five Central Asian countries on joint research and technical training in cotton breeding, high-yield cultivation and water-saving irrigation, while promoting standardized technical guidelines in English and Russian. The Uzbek demonstration field is one place where the results of this cooperation can be seen in the crop itself. Across Central Asia, Chinese cotton expertise is increasingly arriving not as a single product, but as a combination of seeds, farming techniques and machinery. ■

item.title: China's anti-desertification solutions contribute to a greener world
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
ULAN BATOR, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- A giant panda sculpture welcomes visitors to the "China Pavilion" at the ongoing 17th session of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) in Ulan Bator, Mongolia's capital. Inside, photographs, videos and exhibits tell a story that stretches far beyond the pavilion -- how China has been battling desertification at home and is now sharing that experience with countries facing similar challenges. From restoring degraded grasslands to curbing desert expansion, China's experience is drawing growing international attention, while its technologies, expertise and approaches are finding applications across borders. CHINA'S DESERTIFICATION BATTLE One of the countries most severely affected by desertification, China has vast arid heartlands spanning the northwest, north, and northeast, leading Beijing to launch the "Three-North" Shelterbelt Forest Program in 1978 to curb the spread of deserts and restore degraded land. Since the launch of the program, forest and grass coverage across project areas has reached 40.76 percent, and 67.82 percent of treatable sandy land has been brought under control. Since 2021, China has restored over 15 million hectares of degraded grassland, and close to 81 million hectares of grassland have recovered through grazing bans and enclosure measures. Moreover, China's desertification-control efforts in multiple regions have delivered both ecological benefits and tangible gains, including economic returns, for local people in recent years. Since launching a critical-phase battle to advance the "Three-North" program in 2023, through work-for-relief programs, some 1.526 million farmers and herdsmen have secured jobs close to their homes. A total of 100 projects integrating ecological conservation and industrial development have been carried out. The total output value of forest and grass industries in project areas has exceeded 800 billion yuan (about 119.04 billion U.S. dollars). Some 3,528 kilometers of desert-crossing highways have been built, bringing 6.8 million mu (about 453,333 hectares) of desert land under control and opening up roads for local farmers and herdsmen to pursue development and prosperity. In just a few decades, China has evolved from a recipient of international green aid into a major global provider of land restoration expertise, becoming the world's first country to reverse land degradation and shrink its desert footprint. "China is among the most successful nations in desertification control over the past four decades," said Mishal Al-Fawaz, director of the Environment Protection Directorate of Zarqa Governorate, Jordan, citing the "Three-North" Shelterbelt Forest Program. Yasmine Fouad, the UNCCD executive secretary who visited China in July, said: "China has become one of the clearest large-scale examples of how land degradation can be reversed." LESSONS FOR THE WORLD Nasser Bouchiba, president of the Africa-China Cooperation Association for Development in Morocco, said China's achievements in desertification control reflect not only its technological innovation capacity, but also its governance philosophy of harmony between humanity and nature, balancing ecological protection with economic development. "Our biggest source of confidence in desertification prevention and control comes from the people-centered philosophy. This approach constitutes our most fundamental advantage," said Jia Xiaoxia, deputy director of the desertification prevention and control department at China's National Forestry and Grassland Administration. Jia said the advantage has three dimensions: sustained and stable funding to ensure uninterrupted restoration work, long-term holistic planning that enables consistent efforts across generations, and an integrated governance approach that takes into account mountains, rivers, forests, farmlands, lakes, grasslands and sand lands, rather than pursuing isolated, single-track measures. "Jordan can draw lessons from China's experience in long-term planning, community participation, integrating environmental protection with economic development, leveraging technology and scientific research, and sustained government support," said Al-Fawaz. "China's experience demonstrates that when restoration is integrated into broader development planning, environmental action becomes an investment in people and prosperity," Fouad said. "As we move toward COP17, the priority is to translate practical experience like this into stronger cooperation, greater investment and faster implementation, because the scale of land degradation and drought today requires stronger and more coordinated action," she said ahead of the conference. TAKING CHINA'S EXPERIENCE GLOBAL Chinese expertise is empowering desertification-control work in many parts of the world. The country's international cooperation framework on desertification now covers policy and governance experience transfer, talent training and capacity-building, technical cooperation, scientific research innovation, and global governance, among others, said Jia. In Mongolia, China has established ecological restoration demonstration zones, shared practical techniques for planting trees and controlling sand, provided support for saplings, monitored sand and dust, and exchanged knowledge to enhance Mongolia's land rehabilitation efforts. Meanwhile, China runs international workshops to train desert-control professionals for other nations. It has set up cooperation platforms for China-Arab, China-Mongolia and China-Central Asia anti-desertification work, as well as the Northeast Asia network on desertification, land degradation and drought. In July, the UNCCD launched the Business for Land China Hub with the China National Sand Control and Desert Industry Society in Beijing, which will help mobilize Chinese enterprises to engage in global land restoration efforts and share China's desertification-control experience. Sheradil Baktygulov, director of the Institute of World Politics of Kyrgyzstan, noted that China's desertification-control assistance is no empty rhetoric but delivers tangible outcomes. Chinese technologies, including drip irrigation, irrigation channel water storage and tree cultivation, are spreading across Central Asia and help curb desert spread, said Baktygulov.■

item.title: Xi advances a shared future with China's neighbors
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Picked fresh in Kyrgyz villages in the morning, cherries and melons can now travel hundreds of kilometers and reach markets in Kashgar, an oasis city in the southwestern corner of China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, by evening. The journey is made possible by the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan highway, which winds through the rugged mountains of Central Asia, a project under the Belt and Road Initiative proposed by Chinese President Xi Jinping. Shipment will be expedited as the three countries are also seeing the construction of another major cross-border project -- the China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway -- aimed at improving the well-being of people along the route. The expanding connectivity across Central Asia offers a glimpse into a broader vision Xi has championed over the years: to pursue friendships and partnerships with China's neighbors and foster an amicable, secure and prosperous neighborhood. Xi will soon pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan, China's neighbor to the west, and attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek, a major move of his neighborhood diplomacy. "WISH OUR NEIGHBORS WELL" Xi's upcoming trip to Kyrgyzstan will be his third visit to the country as Chinese president, following previous visits in 2013 and 2019. Over the years, stronger connectivity has led to expanded economic ties. In 2025, trade in goods between China and Kyrgyzstan reached 27.2 billion U.S. dollars, up 20 percent year-on-year. Last year, Xi and Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov signed a joint statement on deepening the China-Kyrgyzstan comprehensive strategic partnership for a new era, with the two sides pledging to deepen infrastructure cooperation while tapping new potential in clean energy, green minerals and artificial intelligence. The growing partnership has also been reflected in the Kyrgyz leader's words. He told Xi that Kyrgyzstan's most valuable advantage is having China as its neighbor. For Xi, relations with neighboring countries have long occupied a prominent place in China's diplomacy. In 2013, not long after assuming the Chinese presidency, Xi put forward the principle of amity, sincerity, mutual benefit and inclusiveness in China's relations with its neighbors. A year later, he formally proposed building a community with a shared future with neighboring countries at a central conference on work related to foreign affairs in Beijing. "Close neighbors are better than distant relatives. This is a simple truth that Chinese people got to know in ancient times," Xi once said in explaining China's approach to its neighborhood. "We always wish our neighbors well." Harboring that wish, Xi has maintained frequent exchanges with leaders across China's neighborhood. In 2025, all of Xi's overseas trips took him to neighboring countries, including Kazakhstan, Russia and South Korea. Such diplomatic exchanges have remained intensive in 2026. In June, Xi made his first overseas trip this year, traveling to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, China's neighbor to the northeast. So far this year, Xi has hosted leaders from more than 10 neighboring countries across Asia, including Thailand, Pakistan and Tajikistan. When meeting with Bangladeshi Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in June, Xi reiterated China's commitment to the policy of good-neighborliness and friendship. China, Xi said, will continue to provide neighboring countries with new opportunities and fresh dynamism as the country grows. GOOD-NEIGHBORLINESS IN REGIONAL COOPERATION In addition to bilateral efforts, Xi has attached great importance to regional cooperation to build an amicable, secure and prosperous neighborhood. The SCO is a case in point. "China has always prioritized the SCO in its neighborhood diplomacy," Xi once said. Since 2013, he has attended every SCO summit, either in person or via video link, promoting closer cooperation among member states on security, development and cultural exchanges. Founded in Shanghai in 2001 by China and its neighboring countries, the SCO has had good-neighborliness at the heart of its mission from the outset. "We were the first to conclude a treaty on long-term good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, proclaiming our commitment to forge lasting friendship and refrain from hostilities," Xi said while hosting last year's SCO summit in the northern Chinese port city of Tianjin. Over the past 25 years, the SCO has grown into the world's largest comprehensive regional organization in terms of geographical coverage and population, while expanding cooperation across an ever-widening range of fields. At the Tianjin summit, Xi announced three China-SCO cooperation platforms for energy, green industry and the digital economy, along with three cooperation centers for scientific and technological innovation, higher education, and vocational and technical education. Open to all SCO countries, these initiatives seek to share the opportunities created by China's development while fostering sustainable development across the region. The SCO is part of a broader network of multilateral cooperation across China's neighborhood. Under Xi's leadership, China has worked with neighboring countries through mechanisms ranging from Lancang-Mekong Cooperation to ASEAN-centered East Asian cooperation and APEC, promoting greater connectivity, deeper economic integration and closer people-to-people bonds. In Central Asia, that approach has also been advanced through a new cooperation mechanism initiated by Xi. In 2023, he launched the China-Central Asia Summit in the Chinese city of Xi'an, bringing together China and Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Two years later, Xi traveled to Kazakhstan, China's neighbor to the northwest, for the second China-Central Asia Summit. There, the leaders of the six countries signed a treaty on eternal good-neighborliness, friendship and cooperation, enshrining the principle of everlasting friendship in legal form. Xi said the treaty is "a pioneering initiative in China's diplomatic engagement with its neighbors." At the summit, host Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev highlighted China's role in advancing regional cooperation. "We have forged an unprecedented model of cooperation based on good-neighborliness, friendship and mutual support," Tokayev said. "It is fair to say that China, under the leadership of the great statesman President Xi Jinping, has played a leading role." A SHARED FUTURE "Asia is our common home," Xi wrote in a signed article published by Vietnam's Nhan Dan newspaper in 2023 ahead of a visit to the country. "Building a community with a shared future for humanity should start from Asia." That vision has found concrete expression in China's neighborhood diplomacy. In April last year, Xi convened a central conference on work related to neighboring countries in Beijing, where building a community with a shared future with neighboring countries was identified as a priority. To advance that goal, the conference underscored the need for China to work with its neighbors to consolidate strategic mutual trust, support regional countries in pursuing development paths suited to their respective conditions, and properly manage differences. Days later, Xi embarked on a tour of Southeast Asia that took him to Vietnam, Malaysia and Cambodia, during which he elaborated on how China seeks to put that vision into practice. During the visit, China and the three countries signed a record 108 cooperation agreements, covering traditional infrastructure, connectivity and emerging sectors such as the digital economy. China, Xi said, would "extend the benefits of Chinese modernization to its neighbors, promote the building of a community with a shared future with neighboring countries, and work together to advance modernization in Asia." Over the years, the vision has been translated into an expanding web of bilateral and regional cooperation. China has reached common understandings on building communities with a shared future with 17 neighboring countries. At the subregional level, China and the five Mekong countries have agreed to build a Lancang-Mekong community with a shared future, while China and the five Central Asian nations have committed to building a China-Central Asia community with a shared future. Improved connectivity has laid a solid foundation for closer ties. "If the Belt and Road are likened to the two wings of a soaring Asia, then connectivity represents its arteries and veins," Xi once said. China has signed Belt and Road cooperation documents with 25 neighboring states across Asia, while a connectivity network encompassing "six corridors, six routes, and multiple countries and ports" is now largely in place. Roads, railways, ports and trade routes are bringing markets and communities closer together. Xi's vision of a shared future goes beyond regional connectivity; it envisions countries of different sizes and with different national conditions coexisting, cooperating and pursuing shared development on the basis of equality and mutual benefit. China's own modernization has enabled its neighbors to achieve technological advances and industrial upgrading through collaboration, said Wirun Phichaiwongphakdee, director of the Thailand-China Research Center of the Belt and Road Initiative. Xi's neighborhood vision is being translated into reality through concrete projects, helping make Asia a platform for cooperation and shared prosperity, he added. As Xi once put it metaphorically, "Countries across Asia are like individual lamps. Only when they are connected can they illuminate the night sky of Asia in all its brilliance."■

item.title: Iran's president says U.S. to achieve nothing through economic pressure
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
TEHRAN, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said on Wednesday that the United States will not achieve anything through its economic pressure against Iran. He made the remarks at a meeting in the capital Tehran to discuss the latest situation of Iran's major monetary, foreign currency and financial indices. Iran's Minister of Economic Affairs and Finance Seyed Ali Madanizadeh, Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati and a group of prominent economists attended the meeting, according to a statement published on the website of his office. Pezeshkian said that although Iran seeks to resolve issues through engagement and negotiation, it will, at the same time, stand firm against economic pressure, as it has so far. He expressed confidence that the United States will not achieve anything through its economic pressure at this stage, citing preparations made by his administration's economic sectors. He said this would be similar to the (40-day) war, when the Iranian armed forces and people prevented it from attaining its objectives with their bravery and support. Earlier this month, U.S. President Donald Trump announced "the most crushing economic operation ever taken" against any country providing a lifeline to Iran. "This will be Economic Warfare and Isolation on an unprecedented scale," he said, calling the move "an ECONOMIC D-DAY." On Feb. 28, Israel and the United States launched joint attacks on Tehran and other Iranian cities. Iran responded with waves of missile and drone attacks targeting Israel and U.S. bases and assets in the region. On June 18, the United States and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on ending the war in the region on all fronts, including Lebanon. Under the MoU, they were scheduled to hold negotiations within 60 days, which ended on Aug. 17, to reach a final agreement, but the fate of the talks remains unclear following the escalation between the two countries last month. ■

item.title: China unveils roadmap for AI, NEV industrial upgrading
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- China has formulated nearly 200 key artificial intelligence (AI) standards, and plans to build 500 zero-carbon factories and optimize new energy vehicle (NEV) policies during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) to boost industrial upgrading, senior officials said Wednesday. Xin Guobin, vice minister of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT), said at a press conference held by the State Council Information Office that AI has now been largely integrated across the entire industrial chain in China, including research and development, design, production, manufacturing, quality inspection, as well as operations and maintenance. Xin added that multiple cities are being organized to carry out AI ethics reviews and service practices. Liu Yulin, director of the MIIT's information and communications development department, said at the press conference that during the 2026-2030 period, efforts to advance core 6G technologies will be accelerated. Liu said China will continue 6G technology trials and standards development to promote the maturation of the 6G industry and build its ecosystem, preparing for the commercial deployment of 6G. During the 15th Five-Year Plan period, China will establish 500 zero-carbon factories, creating replicable models to advance the green and low-carbon transformation of its industrial sector, according to Xin. During the period, efforts will also be made to promote the high-quality development of the intelligent connected NEV industry, uphold the bottom line of product quality, and improve the safety and reliability of autonomous driving, Xin said. Policies on NEV insurance will be optimized, and maintenance costs will be reduced to address consumer concerns and encourage consumers to purchase and use NEVs with confidence, he added. China's computing power infrastructure continues to be solidified, according to Xin. As of the end of June this year, the country's intelligent computing capacity reached 2,185 EFLOPS, with over 70 major computing corridors established around computing power hubs. EFLOPS, or ExaFLOPS, is a unit of computing performance, with each unit representing 1 quintillion floating-point operations per second. China's open-source large AI models have achieved innovative breakthroughs and delivered cost-effective performance, becoming the preferred choice for an increasing number of global users. Through real-world training, robots have been deployed in operational modes across scenarios such as manufacturing, emergency rescue, and catering services. Many application scenarios were vividly demonstrated at the recently concluded 2026 World Robot Conference, which lasted from Aug. 19 to 23 in Beijing. The ongoing World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, held from Aug. 22 to 26, also saw unprecedented ticket demand and huge attendance. The recently released action plan on international AI ethics governance has received active responses from numerous countries. The action plan was released at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance held in Shanghai in July. Over the next five years, efforts will accelerate to build emerging pillar industries such as integrated circuits, aerospace, biomedicine, the low-altitude economy, novel energy storage, and intelligent robotics, Xin noted. Meanwhile, he added that future industries including quantum technology, biomanufacturing, hydrogen and nuclear fusion energy, brain-computer interfaces, embodied intelligence, and 6G will be promoted as new drivers of economic growth. China will focus on cultivating high-quality enterprises, improving the tiered cultivation system for such enterprises, fostering and strengthening the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that use specialized and sophisticated technologies to produce novel and unique products, according to Xin, adding that the country will foster more "little giant" enterprises with high growth potential, advanced technology and strong market competitive edge as well as more single-product specialists in the manufacturing industry. The country will strive to promote high-quality development in the information and communications industry, accelerate the planning and construction of next-generation communication networks and computing power networks, promote large-scale application of 5G and industrial internet in key industries, strengthen the research and development of 6G technologies, enhance capabilities in network and data security, and consolidate and elevate the industry's competitive advantage and leading position. During the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance last month, China stressed the need for adhering to the principles of openness and win-win and boosting innovation-driven development, strengthening risk awareness and ensuring that AI is secure and controllable, encouraging inclusiveness and promoting mutual learning between civilizations, and advocating solidarity and improving global governance. China is a global leader in AI development. In 2025, its core AI industries were worth over 1.2 trillion yuan (about 176.6 billion U.S. dollars), while the number of AI enterprises nationwide exceeded 6,200. ■

item.title: Xi to attend SCO summit, pay state visit to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- From Aug. 30 to Sept. 3, Chinese President Xi Jinping will attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and pay a state visit to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt upon the invitation of President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan and President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt, the Chinese foreign ministry announced on Wednesday. This year marks the 25th founding anniversary of the SCO. At the Bishkek Summit, Xi will have in-depth exchanges of views with participating leaders on deepening SCO cooperation in various fields under the new circumstances and major international and regional issues, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian told a regular news briefing when asked for more information about the trip. They will provide guidance for the SCO's high-quality development and participation in the reform and development of the global governance system, Lin said. During his stay in Kyrgyzstan, Xi will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations, cooperation in key areas, and international and regional situation with his Kyrgyz counterpart in their talks, and attend various state events, Lin noted. Lin said China looks forward to working with Kyrgyzstan to take this visit as an opportunity to promote high-quality development of mutually beneficial cooperation on all fronts, add new dimensions to the China-Kyrgyzstan community with a shared future, and bring more benefits to the two peoples. The Egypt leg of Xi's trip, his first state visit to the country in a decade, coincides with the 70th anniversary of bilateral diplomatic ties, the spokesperson said. The Chinese and Egyptian presidents will have an in-depth exchange of views on bilateral relations and international and regional issues of mutual interest, according to Lin. Through the visit, China looks forward to working with Egypt to carry forward traditional friendship, render each other firm support, expand mutually beneficial cooperation, and bolster each other's modernization, thereby jointly drawing a new chapter of bilateral relations and contributing to regional and world peace and stability, Lin added. ■

item.title: Xi urges all-out rescue, relief efforts after mudslide hits border port in Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 26 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has ordered all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing after a mudslide in Nepal caused casualties at Gyirong border port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday morning. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, called for efforts to evacuate residents at risk and provide timely medical treatment to the injured to minimize casualties. He made the instructions after a mudslide occurred at around 10:30 a.m. on Wednesday in Nepal, which caused severe casualties and left people unaccounted for at Gyirong border port in Gyirong County. Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Noting that China is currently in a critical period of flood control, he urged local authorities and relevant departments to prepare for worst-case scenarios and extreme situations, fully implement measures for flood and typhoon prevention, and step up efforts to identify and address potential risks and hazards. He demanded resolute action to prevent major and catastrophic disasters and accidents and safeguard people's lives and property. Premier Li Qiang also issued instructions, calling for an immediate verification of the number of the missing and affected people and for all-out rescue and relief efforts. Li, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, instructed the Foreign Ministry to strengthen communication and coordination with relevant countries, promptly share information and work together to properly handle rescue and relief efforts. Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing, also a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, led officials from relevant departments to the site to guide rescue and disaster-response operations. Authorities in Xizang have mobilized forces to carry out search and rescue operations. All relevant operations are underway. ■
